gloss: fine piece of music; excellent song

definitions.gloss: fine piece of music; excellent song; good composition
definitions.explanation: A musical piece of high quality or artistic merit. A somewhat formal and appreciative term used in music criticism and reviews to praise a composition without the superlative force of 'masterpiece.'

examples.japanese: このアルバムには{佳曲|かきょく}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: This album has many fine songs.

examples.japanese: {隠|かく}れた{佳曲|かきょく}を{集|あつ}めたプレイリストを{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made a playlist of hidden gems.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{初期|しょき}の{作品|さくひん}には、{今|いま}でも{色褪|いろあ}せない{佳曲|かきょく}が{数多|かずおお}く{含|ふく}まれている。
examples.english: Among his early works, there are many fine pieces that have not faded with time.

notes:
Composed of {佳|か} (good, fine, beautiful) and {曲|きょく} (piece of music, tune). The character {佳|か} implies refined, understated quality rather than overwhelming greatness. This word is frequently used in music reviews, liner notes, and critical writing. It carries a tone of genuine but measured praise.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {隠|かく}れた{佳曲|かきょく}: hidden gem (in music)
- {佳曲|かきょく}{揃|ぞろ}い: full of fine songs
- {知|し}られざる{佳曲|かきょく}: an unknown fine piece

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {名曲|めいきょく}: masterpiece, famous piece — implies greater fame and recognition
- {良曲|りょうきょく}: good song — more casual and used more in informal online discussion
- {秀曲|しゅうきょく}: excellent piece — emphasizes outstanding quality; rarer
